items.title: Here’s what happened in crypto today

items.title: Ledger hardware implant saga reaches Dubai’s Virgin Megastore
items.excerpt: Two Ledger owners reported losing a combined $604,000 in crypto from hardware wallets they said were purchased at authorized retailer Virgin Megastore in Dubai.

items.title: Nvidia’s startup stakes ballooned to $65B, but Huang’s exit puts future deals in doubt
items.excerpt: The value of Nvidia’s private investments has nearly tripled over the past nine months, fueled by Jensen Huang’s aggressive dealmaking and rising valuations of its existing portfolio companies.

items.title: Nvidia promises that revenue will keep soaring — for now
items.excerpt: Despite the turmoil Nvidia is in after the departure of its disgraced founder and CEO Jensen Huang, the company projected that its streak of record-breaking revenue isn't about to stop.

items.title: Nvidia board rejects Huang comeback despite record $116B quarter
items.excerpt: Nvidia beat Wall Street’s revenue expectations by 5.6% and issued a stronger-than-expected sales forecast, while its board resisted growing calls for Jensen Huang’s reinstatement.

items.title: Stripe backer Atomico calls for Europe to own its success stories

items.excerpt: Sidney Powell aims to reach $15 billion in assets under management by the end of 2027 as the firm looks to expand into tokenized lending and traditional finance.

items.title: SEC reportedly investigating Nvidia amid Huang exit
items.excerpt: The SEC is opening a probe into Nvidia following the departure of CEO Jensen Huang, who admitted to an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, reports The Wall Street Journal.

items.title: Google joins the tech outage trend by announcing it’s not having one
items.excerpt: With tech outages seemingly everywhere, Google took the unusual step of announcing that Gmail is working just fine, actually.

items.title: Eastern Europe crypto flows fall 7.9% as Ukraine draws $12B in stablecoins
items.excerpt: Chainalysis found that Eastern Europe recorded the steepest decline in crypto activity of any region, while cross-border stablecoin transfers to Ukraine continued amid the ongoing war.

items.title: Waymo suspends freeway rides nationwide after California DMV order
items.excerpt: The DMV said Waymo's freeway operations pose an imminent hazard to public safety. Restrictions will remain in place until Waymo can demonstrate that it has taken "effective corrective actions" to address the deficiencies.

items.title: Model ML raises $250M to automate investment banking grunt work
items.excerpt: The startup says its agents understand the full context of deals that bankers and consultants are working on and can automatically update financial models and presentations when new developments affect their analysis.

items.title: Google expands access to Gemini Tasks, which can help with calls, purchases
items.excerpt: Gemini's Task mode can help users coordinate calls, log into websites, and even make purchases on the user's behalf.

items.title: Apple services, including iCloud, App Store, Apple Music, and more, hit by outage
items.excerpt: Apple's status page confirms its services are facing outages, but has not confirmed the cause.

items.title: Google to keep Gemini chats for 2 months, up from 72 hours, even with history off
items.excerpt: Google's Gemini update extending chat retention will roll out globally over the coming weeks.

items.title: As decision model use skyrockets, is customization the next frontier?
items.excerpt: Sqwish Labs has a new wrinkle on the decision model: Train it with your own data to max its capabilities.

items.title: Pedestal AI raises $4.7 million to agentify the supply chain
items.excerpt: The company uses agentic AI to make supply chains faster and more reliable.

items.title: Lighter incident exposes risks beyond withdrawal controls
items.excerpt: Crypto platforms need enforceable limits on every route an API key can use to transfer value, including trades, internal transfers and shared pools.

items.title: Fed’s Waller cites Binance hack in warning over tokenized finance
items.excerpt: Fed Governor Christopher Waller questioned who bears responsibility for fraud, compromised keys and failed transactions as traditional financial assets move onto blockchains.

items.title: Proton’s Lumo, a privacy-focused alternative to ChatGPT and Claude, arrives on desktop
items.excerpt: Proton's new Lumo Desktop app for Windows, Mac, and Linux lets users automate tasks across files and connected apps, with granular controls over what its AI can access.

items.excerpt: In the first public statement since his resignation, Nvidia founder Jensen Huang signaled his willingness to return as CEO.

items.title: Bitcoin drops 2.5% as Nvidia stock risks new 5-month lows into Q3 earnings
items.excerpt: Bitcoin price downside sees local lows of $63,269 as Nvidia stock targets $150 as traders brace for volatility over Q3 earnings.

items.title: Daydream’s new AI agent acts as your personal stylist — and can shop for you, too
items.excerpt: Daydream's new AI shopping agent can remember your style, virtually try on clothes, plan outfits around your wardrobe, track sales, and complete purchases.

items.title: Solana Foundation takes majority interest in crypto data firm CoinGecko
items.excerpt: Solana Foundation now holds a majority interest in CoinGecko, its product chief said, as the crypto data platform explores trading features.

items.title: Bitcoin to $1M by 2030? ‘Almost certainly not,’ says Dragonfly’s Qureshi
items.excerpt: Dragonfly’s Haseeb Qureshi says Bitcoin could reach $400,000 by 2030 but doubts it will return to $100,000 by year-end with the rout in AI stocks weighing on crypto.

items.title: ARK sells $85M in Nvidia shares ahead of chipmaker’s Q3 earnings results
items.excerpt: ARK bought shares in Block, Circle and Coinbase worth about $39.9 million at Monday’s close while selling Nvidia and Solana and Ether staking ETFs.

items.title: Revolut plans four blockchain-based funds for private markets, chair says
items.excerpt: Citing a looming liquidity crunch, Martin Gilbert said blockchain could help bring more liquidity to private markets.

items.title: US senators seek SEC answers on tokenized stock money laundering risks
items.excerpt: Four Democratic senators asked who would be responsible for tokenized shares transferred outside regulated platforms and whether the SEC could freeze or recover those tokens.

items.title: BlackRock’s Bitcoin ETF snaps $2.35B outflow streak amid extreme fear
items.excerpt: BlackRock’s Bitcoin ETF ended 11 sessions of withdrawals totaling $2.35 billion, but CryptoQuant says one day of inflows is too early to signal a recovery.

items.title: Bitcoin realized loss metric beats June high as open interest eyes 2-year low
items.excerpt: Bitcoin short-term holders’ onchain spending notched the largest proportion of realized losses since February after BTC/USD dropped to $62,000.

items.title: Google says hackers use AI agents to find and exploit software flaws
items.excerpt: Google says attackers are using AI agents to find and exploit software flaws automatically, reducing the time organizations have to apply patches.

items.title: US judge clears brothers in $25M Ethereum MEV case after mistrial
items.excerpt: Judge Jessica Clarke said the transactions did not involve false promises, but the ruling did not determine whether the brothers’ conduct was ethical or violated other laws.

items.title: Goldman Sachs reports $1.22B in Ether ETFs as ETHA share count jumps
items.excerpt: Goldman Sachs increased its Ether ETF shares in Q3, bringing its reported holdings to $1.22 billion, while reshuffling its Bitcoin ETF positions.

items.title: Ex-Robinhood engineer pleads guilty to $125K Hyperliquid trading scheme
items.excerpt: The former Robinhood engineer used confidential information about upcoming Robinhood token listings to trade on Hyperliquid.

items.title: Trezor customer data exposed in 3rd partner breach this year
items.excerpt: Trezor warned an attacker has been able to access customer names, phone numbers and delivery addresses linked to 27,000 orders from one of its shipping providers.

items.title: Hackers inject credit card, crypto-stealing malware into 178 major websites
items.excerpt: Ledger and Coinpass were among the businesses whose websites served malware designed to steal visitors’ crypto and credit card details, according to security researchers.

items.title: Nvidia shares fall 4% as board reportedly rules out Huang return
items.excerpt: The chipmaker’s board is reportedly focused on investigating Huang’s conduct, even as a petition calling for his reinstatement gathers more than 187,000 signatures.

items.title: Custodia Bank loses Supreme Court bid for direct Fed payment access
items.excerpt: The Supreme Court refused to hear Custodia Bank’s appeal, meaning a lower court ruling allowing the Fed to reject account applications will stand.

items.title: German lawmakers back crypto freezes outside criminal cases
items.excerpt: Customs authorities could hold “suspicious” assets for 30 days under the bill, with court oversight for extensions and disputed confiscation.

items.title: Binance hack may push institutions to outside custody, FalconX exec says
items.excerpt: FalconX’s Joshua Lim says the Binance hack could push institutions to keep crypto off exchanges and change how large investors trade in 2027.

items.title: Bitmine edges toward 5% of ETH supply as treasuries report buys amid market slump
items.excerpt: Strategy, Strive, Bitmine and Cypherpunk disclosed fresh additions to their crypto treasuries, spanning Bitcoin, Ether and Zcash.

items.title: Boris Johnson says UK must lead blockchain development despite crypto doubts
items.excerpt: Johnson was joined by Lord Ross Kempsell who called for regulators to work with industry participants to bring the UK to the forefront.

items.title: Coinbase and Broadridge propose standard for tokenized stock disclosures
items.excerpt: The proposed standard aims to connect tokenized stockholders with corporate disclosures and voting materials across digital wallets, but would not create shareholder rights.

items.title: Nvidia turmoil tests Bitcoin miners’ AI funding plans
items.excerpt: Nvidia’s leadership upheaval and Texas permit restrictions sharpen the divide between miners with funded projects and those still seeking capital and approvals.
